chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam al-Asadi, from Abu Hamza, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, the tongue of the son of Adam stands over all his limbs every morning, and it says, 'How have you fared?' So they say, 'With goodness, if you leave us,' and they say, 'Allah, Allah, regarding us,' and they adjure it, and they say, 'We are rewarded and punished only because of you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the tongue in Islamic ethics according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this vivid metaphor from *Al-Kafi*, the tongue is depicted as the sovereign overseer of the body, holding the power of life and death for the other limbs through its speech. The dialogue illustrates the Shia understanding of accountability, where the tongue acts as the primary agent of reward or punishment, emphasizing that silence is often the most effective means of preserving the integrity of the entire self. This narration underscores the practical ethical imperative of guarding one's speech as a means of safeguarding one's spiritual fate.
